A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeDART, with matching architecture, datasets and retained experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original forecasting and classification experiments, backbone comparisons, ablations and hyperparameter analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and adds few-shot, linear-probing, input-length and computational-efficiency results.

M1.justification: The patch embedding, causal encoder, independent patch noising, masked denoising decoder and diffusion objective remain unchanged. v5 explicitly formulates the output projector in Equation 8, but v3 already describes this linear projection. Linear probing is an added evaluation protocol.

E1.justification: The forecasting and classification datasets, domains and tasks are retained. The added analyses change training fractions, encoder freezing and look-back lengths within existing coverage. Appendix A corrects '6' classification datasets to '3'; both versions actually evaluate HAR, Epilepsy and EEG.

E2.justification: The evaluated baseline suite is retained, and the new analyses reuse existing comparators. Table 7 newly displays random-initialization references, but v3 already discusses the noise-scheduler comparison against random initialization in Section 4.4 and includes forecasting reference results in Table 15.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 adds evaluation using 5%/10% of training data with the complete test set, frozen-encoder linear probing, and look-back-length sweeps. Appendix G adds a Traffic computational-cost comparison at L = H = 336. These substantially extend evaluation design; existing benchmark splits and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds analyses of label efficiency, representation quality with a frozen encoder, sensitivity to longer input windows, and computational cost. These address additional questions beyond v3's retained component ablations, decoder/patch/noise sensitivity studies and forecasting showcases.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The new results continue reporting point estimates and averages across prediction horizons without introducing a documented uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and appendix result values are retained, while Table 8, Figure 6 and Tables 20–22 add substantial results under new protocols. For example, linear-probing ETTh2 MSE is 0.354 for TimeDART, 0.357 for SimMTM and 0.361 for TimeMAE. New few-shot reporting contains an inconsistency: ETTh2's 5% MSE is 0.365 in Table 8 versus 0.356 in Table 20.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds the MSE–Gaussian likelihood argument. Appendix C.3 replaces v3's abbreviated ELBO-to-loss argument with explicit variational decomposition, Gaussian transition assumptions and KL calculations. It also corrects the sign of log(q/p) in the bound. This substantially expands mathematical reasoning without changing the final training objective.

C1.justification: The abstract and three contribution bullets retain the same claims about unifying autoregressive and diffusion modeling, capturing global/local patterns, and outperforming baselines across nine datasets. The added concluding sentence summarizes further evidence for already claimed adaptability and robustness.

C2.justification: v5 expands the Gaussian-versus-multimodal motivation and interprets the new analyses as evidence of label efficiency and transferable representations. It attributes longer-input gains to noise mitigation and computational efficiency to avoiding lengthy sampling. Appendix G also introduces overly universal outperformance interpretations despite ties and exceptions in its tables.

D1.justification: Table 22 newly reports parameter counts and per-epoch training times, including TimeDART's 2.36M pre-training parameters and 510-second pre-training epochs on Traffic. Classification captions specify Macro-F1 where v3 says F1. Hardware, existing hyperparameters and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds targeted references, including Chen et al. on diffusion representations, Li et al. on autoregressive image generation, Cheng et al.'s forecasting survey and Vaswani et al.; Luo (2022) is removed. The main research positioning remains stable. Numerous other reference edits are publication updates rather than different cited works.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the introduction, related work, patching explanation and experimental-fairness discussion, alongside terminology and grammar edits. v5 adds analysis subsections and acknowledgments and updates author/header text, while retaining the overall narrative and section sequence.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive localized presentation revisions, Table 7 is reformatted, and v5 adds Figure 6 and Tables 8 and 20–22. Existing charts and detailed result tables are retained; the forecasting showcase moves from Figure 6 to Figure 7. The overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's full-fine-tuning evidence, the added frozen-encoder and limited-label evaluations provide more direct support for representation quality, while measured costs clarify practicality. These gains are limited by new reporting problems: the ETTh2 discrepancy between Tables 8 and 20 and Appendix G's universal outperformance claims despite ties and a worse PEMS04 few-shot MAE. Overall, the additions improve evidential coverage modestly without resolving all reporting weaknesses.
